note: Do one thing today: one action per day, chosen by date (days since 2026-01-01 UTC-10, mod list length). Every URL checked 2026-10-11. Edit here, then run scripts/weekly-sync.sh (it renders the list into the HTML so /fr/ /es/ /ar/ get translations).

actions.text: Snap a photo of the sky and send it to NASA's GLOBE Observer app to help check cloud data from satellites.
Spot an aurora? Report it to Aurorasaurus so scientists can map where it showed up.
Spend 10 minutes hunting for cold worlds near the Sun with Backyard Worlds: Planet 9.
Look through telescope data for new planets with Planet Hunters TESS.
Browse NASA's citizen-science projects and pick one you can do from your couch.
Help map kelp forests by marking them on satellite images with Floating Forests.
Find a coastal cleanup near you on Ocean Conservancy's cleanup map.
Download the Clean Swell app and log every piece of trash you pick up.
Pick up 10 pieces of litter on your street and log them in Marine Debris Tracker.
Learn how trash ends up in the ocean and how to stop it at the source.
Find a Surfrider beach cleanup near you.
Join or start a Great American Cleanup event in your town.
Live near the Great Lakes? Adopt a beach and clean it a few times a year.
Check how to recycle common items the right way where you live.
Look for the WaterSense label next time you replace a faucet, shower head or toilet.
Look for the ENERGY STAR label next time you buy a light bulb or appliance.
Photograph a plant or animal outside and share it on iNaturalist to help scientists track nature.
Count the birds you see for 15 minutes and submit your list to eBird.
Read how cities are keeping trash out of rivers and oceans.
In New York City? Sign up to help restore oysters in the harbor.
In Baltimore? Volunteer with the Mr. Trash Wheel team.
See how you can help Great Lakes Plastic Cleanup catch plastic in marinas.
Chip in to help The Ocean Cleanup remove plastic from oceans and rivers.
Help plant trees across Europe with Life Terra.
Help grow and replant coral on Florida's reefs.
Mark World Cleanup Day on your calendar and find an event near you.
Can't find a cleanup? Start your own with Ocean Conservancy's free guide.
